Subject: DPA questions for private deployment (cust-managed keys + operator access)

Hi Ethan —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal and Security at MediCore have a few follow-ups before we move forward with the private deployment:

1) We want the DPA to explicitly reflect that MediCore will hold and control the master key (customer-managed keystore) and that Redwood will not have the ability to decrypt customer data outside of ephemeral support workflows.
2) We need clarity on the operator telemetry that Redwood collects from private deployments (agent logs, invocation traces, runtime metrics). Can you provide a scope and retention for anything that could be considered customer data?
3) Subprocessors: please confirm which infrastructure partners will process logs or telemetry for private deployments and whether any cross-border transfers are involved.

Can you send a short addendum we can share with legal + our security team? Attachments or a one-pager would be ideal.

Appreciate it,
Claire O'Neill
Head of Platform Security — MediCore
claire.oneill@medicore.com

Subject: Re: DPA questions for private deployment (cust-managed keys + operator access)

Claire —

Thanks for the clear list. I chatted with Legal and Security here and attached a concise DPA addendum draft that addresses: customer-managed keys, explicit breakglass support flow, operator telemetry scoping, and a subprocessors appendix. Highlights below:

- Keystore custody: customer retains master key (we support customer-managed KMS or HSM). Redwood will only hold short-lived wrapping keys for routing when explicitly requested by the customer and only under documented, auditable breakglass procedures.
- Operator access: runtime operator access is scoped to orchestration and node-level health telemetry. No user prompts or model payloads are included in routine telemetry. Any access to decrypted inputs/outputs requires an approval chain (customer security approved ticket + time-limited signed consent).
- Telemetry retention: default telemetry retention for private deployments is 30 days; extended retention requires a customer contract addendum.
- Subprocessors: list included in appendix; for private deployments, the typical subprocessors are our monitoring SaaS (metrics ingest for Dedicated control plane), the cloud provider (if deployed in a managed VPC), and our build artifact CDN. We flag any cross-border transfer in the appendix — for MediCore's US region deploy there are no EU transfers expected.

I'm attaching: redwood-dpa-addendum-keystore-20260621.pdf (draft addendum), keystore-handshake-matrix-20260621.xlsx (detailed ops demarcation), and operator-telemetry-boundary.txt (plain text summary).

If helpful I can set up a 30-min walkthrough with your security and legal folks later this week.

Best,
Ethan Park

Thanks for the fast turn. A few clarifying asks from our side after a quick read:
- The addendum references a "wrapping key" usage by Redwood for routing. Can you clarify what material is wrapped vs. what is exclusively under our HSM? We need to ensure private model inputs/outputs never leave the customer KMS unwrapped.
- On telemetry: your note says "node-level health telemetry" — can you list concrete metrics included (e.g., CPU/gpu, process restarts, kernel panics) and confirm that any application-level logs (prompts, outputs) are excluded from aggregation pipelines by default?
- For the subprocessors appendix: can you confirm whether your monitoring SaaS (the hosted ingest pipeline) ever sees raw telemetry or only aggregated metrics?

Would prefer answers inlined in the addendum or a short follow-up email we can attach to our vendor review.

Subject: Re: DPA questions for private deployment (cust-managed keys + operator access)

David / Claire / Ethan —

Looping in more detail from Legal/Privacy perspective. Inline answers below (we'll update the PDF and push a revision):

1) Wrapping key model: the customer's master key (CMK) lives in the customer's KMS/HSM and is used to decrypt data locally. Redwood will not possess the unwrapped CMK. For routing between private control plane components (when customers opt for our managed control plane), we may use a short-lived wrapping key that encrypts institution-level metadata (instance IDs, scheduling headers) — not customer payloads. We will update the addendum to explicitly state "no model inputs/outputs are wrapped by Redwood-held keys."

2) Telemetry specifics (default collection):
- Included: node metrics (CPU, GPU utilization), process health (uptime, restarts), agent heartbeat, OS-level kernel logs limited to non-user-space stack traces, anonymized aggregate request rates and tail latency percentiles.
- Excluded by default: application payloads (prompts, full model outputs, raw request/response bodies), customer identifiers in logs (we mask request IDs in control-plane telemetry).
- Access controls: any request to access runtime payloads for debugging must originate from a named Redwood engineer, be approved by Redwood Security, and have customer authorization in the form of a signed support ticket. Access is time-limited and audited.

3) Subprocessors: our monitoring SaaS only receives aggregated metrics (time-series, histograms) and does not receive raw payloads. For managed VPC deployments where telemetry must remain in-customer, we offer a private metrics-forwarding option so that the ingest pipeline lives in the customer's account. We'll call out the cloud providers as infrastructure subprocessors and confirm no cross-border transfer for the US-region deployment.

I'll spearhead a tracked change to the addendum and send v2 by EOD.

— Priyo Das
Privacy & Security Program Manager — Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com

David / Claire —

Quick operational clarifications (also pushed into the drive doc):
- No customer payloads will be encrypted with Redwood-held keys. The wrapping key is only for control-plane routing metadata and cannot decrypt model content. We'll add a short paragraph in the addendum with a simple diagram.
- Telemetry list (concrete): GPU temp, GPU utilization per worker, host CPU, oom/killed process events, agent heartbeat, request per-second aggregates, 50/90/99 latency percentiles. No request bodies, prompt texts, or model outputs are emitted.
- Monitoring SaaS: only accepts anonymized metrics in our standard setup. For MediCore we recommend the private metrics-forwarding option (your preferred choice per the earlier call).
